description: ZipDMA F6 declaration for a four-word transfer at one-byte beat size: the control-status bits the completion criterion reads, and the block length the run executes.
notes: dma_transfer_size_bytes 1 in the scenario selects ZipDMA size code 3 in both the source and destination size fields (third_party/soc-zipcpu/rtl/zipdma/zipdma_ctrl.v:119-129,246-252), so the plan's start word is 0x00330000 instead of 0x00000000

with a one-byte beat size the pinned ZipDMA issues one lane beat per byte: mwb_sel carries 1, 2, 4, 8 for the four bytes of each word (third_party/soc-zipcpu/rtl/zipdma/zipdma_mm2s.v:528-544,611-626 and zipdma_s2mm.v:205-233,369-391).  A four-word block therefore completes as 16 source beats and 16 destination beats, which is what the scenario's dma_observation_expectations states

the host applies each declared lane mask with Memory::write's byte enables, so the destination word is assembled from the device's own strobes; the host never re-writes a full word to make the comparison succeed
the block stays four words: this file describes the byte-enable increment, not a longer block (configs/behaviors/zipdma_len8_f6.json states the eight-word declaration)

busy_bit 31 and err_bit 30 are the ZipDMA CONTROL_STATUS bits (third_party/soc-zipcpu/rtl/zipdma/zipdma_ctrl.v:116-117); declaring them states where the completion criterion reads, not that any run observed them
no transfer, completion, IRQ or RTL run is claimed by this declaration
